blocks.content: The National Food Security Act, 2013 marks a paradigm shift in the approach to food security—moving from a traditional welfare approach to a rights-based entitlement system.

rows: Focused strictly on estimated BPL population
Per person allocation (5 kg/person for PHH, 35 kg/family for AAY)

items: Coverage percentages under NFSA 2013 (75% Rural, 50% Urban, 67% Overall) are frequently asked in UPSC and State PSC exams.
Entitlement distinction: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households get 35 kg per household per month, whereas Priority Households (PHH) receive 5 kg per person per month.
Nodal central agency: Food Corporation of India (FCI) is responsible for procurement, storage, and inter-state transportation of PDS food grains.
ONORC scheme enables migrant workers to lift their entitled food grains from any Fair Price Shop (FPS) across India using technology and biometrics.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Public Distribution System (PDS) evolved from a general scarcity-management system into a targeted food security mechanism.
The Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) was launched in June 1997 to focus benefits specifically on Below Poverty Line (BPL) families.
The National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 converted food security from a welfare-based scheme into a legal entitlement.
NFSA legally covers up to 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population under two categories: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) and Priority Households (PHH).
Technological reforms such as One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC), Aadhaar seeding, and Electronic Point of Sale (ePoS) devices have digitized and modernized PDS operation.
